headline: Ratchet & Clank's source becomes easier to navigate without losing matches
summary: Contributors can work with named game states, buttons, levels and shared structures instead of repeated numeric offsets and private declarations. The final snapshot still reports 100% matched code by size, with all 5,116 functions matching the original game's bytes; the refactor preserves the compiled results. Data generated locally from the contributor's own disc now builds through C, with 516,916 of 699,072 data bytes recorded as done.
highlights: The 231,369 additions and 208,167 deletions largely reflect formatting: #169 alone adds 169,328 and deletes 147,550 lines without changing loaded bytes.
Shared headers and system folders make the source easier to find; views that would change the compiled bytes remain private (#174, #191, #192).
Data conversion rises from 0.57% to about 74% across #196, #197 and #198; retail values are generated locally rather than committed.
Match-preserving checks reject regressions, while compiler-sensitive constructs that remain necessary carry reasons (#194, #195, #204). The level extraction issue #165 closed.
